issues.title: [BUG]: `go.Scatter` with `fill="toself"` has broken hover position when used with `rangeslider`.
issues.body:
### Description

If one use `go.Scatter` with `fill="toself"` and `rangeslider`, and output to html, then resulting html will have broken hover system. The `name` of the `trace` should display the hover text when the mouse is within the area of the trace. However, the actual area responses to hover is much smaller in the vertical direction. Also, after zooming, the responsive area to hover is not updated.

### Steps to reproduce

The following works well.
```python
import plotly.graph_objects as go

fig = go.Figure()

fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x=[0, 0, 1, 1],
        y=[1, 0, 0, 1],
        mode="none",
        fill="toself",
        name="AAA",
        showlegend=False,
    ),
)

fig.update_xaxes(range=[-5, 5])

fig.write_html("test.html")
```
But the following has a broken hover system.
```python
import plotly.graph_objects as go

fig = go.Figure()

fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x=[0, 0, 1, 1],
        y=[1, 0, 0, 1],
        mode="none",
        fill="toself",
        name="AAA",
        showlegend=False,
    ),
)

fig.update_xaxes(rangeslider_visible=True, range=[-5, 5])

fig.write_html("test.html")
```
If you zoom in the page, the responsive area of hovering is not updated.
issues.author: ljw20180420

comments.body:
I can reproduce this with plotly 7.1.0 (bundled plotly.js 4.1.1, Python 3.13, Linux) in both Chromium 156 and Firefox 157. I hovered over the middle of the square (x=0.5) at several heights with Playwright:

| | y=0.05 | 0.25 | 0.5 | 0.75 | 0.95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no rangeslider | hover | hover | hover | hover | hover |
| `rangeslider_visible=True` | – | – | – | – | hover |
| same, after `relayout` zoom | – | – | – | – | – |

It looks like the same bug as plotly/plotly.js#7039, and the cause is in plotly.js. The rangeslider draws its mini plot by calling the same scatter `plotOne` (`src/traces/scatter/plot.js`) with `plotinfo.isRangePlot: true`. That second pass overwrites `trace._fillElement` and `trace._polygons` (lines 194, 269-270, 412-413, 430, 445-447 on master) with the rangeslider's own fill path. Fill hover (`isHoverPointInFillElement` in `scatter/hover.js`) then tests the cursor against that small path. You can see it in `gd._fullData[0]._polygons`: with the slider its y-extent is 4–74 px, which is the 78 px slider, while the main plot area spans 21–390 px. That's why only a thin strip near the top responds, and why zooming doesn't help: the slider is redrawn too and overwrites them again.

As a check, I patched the bundled plotly.js in the generated HTML so those three assignments are skipped when `plotinfo.isRangePlot` is set. `plotOne` already does that for `node3` vs `nodeRangePlot3`. After the patch, every height in the table showed the hover label in both browsers, before and after zooming, and a point outside the square still showed nothing. I only tested this single `fill="toself"` trace, not `tonext` fills.
comments.author: mohamd764

issues.title: [BUG]: Single-color requests raise ZeroDivisionError in palette helpers
issues.body:
### Description

`sample_colorscale` and `n_colors` raise `ZeroDivisionError` when asked for one color. This breaks palettes sized to a dataset's group count when there is exactly one group. Both helpers divide by the requested count minus one.

Expected: one color from the start of the interval (`low` / `lowcolor`), consistent with their existing first sample.

### Screenshots/Video

The API calls fail before a figure can be created; the output is shown below.

### Steps to reproduce

```python
from plotly.colors import n_colors, sample_colorscale

for label, call in [
    ("sample_colorscale", lambda: sample_colorscale("Viridis", 1)),
    ("n_colors", lambda: n_colors((0, 0, 0), (1, 1, 1), 1)),
]:
    try:
        print(label, call())
    except ZeroDivisionError as error:
        print(label, type(error).__name__, str(error))
```

Actual:
```text
sample_colorscale ZeroDivisionError division by zero
n_colors ZeroDivisionError float division by zero
```

Expected:
```text
sample_colorscale ['rgb(68, 1, 84)']
n_colors [(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)]
```

### Notes

Reproduced with Plotly 7.1.0, current main `3f8a650930feadfdb651cd869ffe3e85fd093885`, Python 3.12.10, Windows amd64. Zero-color requests already return empty lists.

issues.title: [BUG]: Unnecessary `UserWarning` when using `fig.write_image()` with `kaleido.start_sync_server()`
issues.body:
### Description

When using `kaleido.start_sync_server()`, `fig.write_image()` emits a `UserWarning` on every call, even though no `kopts` are specified.
The warning is:

```text
plotly\io\_kaleido.py:185: UserWarning: The kopts argument is ignored if using a server.
  img_bytes = kaleido.calc_fig_sync(
```

The image is generated successfully, but since no `kopts` are specified, it seems that this warning should not be emitted.

It looks like Plotly passes `kopts` to `kaleido.calc_fig_sync()` even when no Kaleido options are specified.

Would it be possible for Plotly to avoid passing `kopts` when no Kaleido options were specified, or otherwise avoid this warning in this case?

### Steps to reproduce

```python
import plotly.express as px
import kaleido

fig = px.line(x=[0, 1], y=[0, 1])

kaleido.start_sync_server()
fig.write_image("a.png")  # success, but UserWarning
kaleido.stop_sync_server()
```

### Notes

- plotly 7.1.0
- kaleido 1.4.0

issues.title: [BUG]: make_subplots drops or misplaces row_titles/column_titles when an edge cell is spanned
issues.body: ### Description Row and column titles are positioned using the subplot in the last column (row titles) or in the top row (column titles). When that cell is empty because another subplot spans into it, the title ends up on the wrong row/column and the last title is dropped. When the subplot in that cell spans several rows, its title is centred across the whole span. ### Screenshots/Video ### Steps to reproduce python from plotly.subplots import make_subplots fig = make_subplots( rows=2, cols=2, specs=[[{"colspan": 2}, None], [{}, {}]], row_titles=["Row A", "Row B"], ) print([(a.text, round(a.y, 3)) for a in fig.layout.annotations]) # Actual: [('Row A', 0.212)] -> "Row A" sits next to row 2 and "Row B" is missing # Expected: [('Row A', 0.787), ('Row B', 0.212)] ### Notes Two more layouts with the same problem: - `specs=[[{}, {"rowspan": 2}], [{}, None]]` with `row_titles=["R1", "R2"]`: R1 is centred across both rows (y=0.5) and R2 is missing. - `specs=[[{"rowspan": 2}, {}], [None, {}]]`, `start_cell="bottom-left"` with `column_titles=["C1", "C2"]`: C1 is drawn over the second column and C2 is missing. The docstring describes `row_titles`/`column_titles` as lists of length `rows`/`cols` with one title per row/column, so I'd expect each title to stay on its own row/column regardless of spans. Reproduces on plotly 7.1.0 and on current main.

issues.title: [BUG]: Integer and string properties reject NumPy scalars
issues.body:
### Description

Graph object properties validated as integers (such as `layout.xaxis.nticks`, `histogram.nbinsx` and `layout.updatemenus[].active`) reject NumPy integer scalars, and properties validated as non-strict strings (such as `name` and `text`) reject NumPy integer and `float32` scalars. Python `int` and `float` values of the same number are accepted, and number properties such as `marker.size` already accept NumPy scalars.

This breaks a common pattern: building one trace per value of a DataFrame column with `Series.unique()`, which returns NumPy scalars.

Expected: NumPy integers are accepted wherever a Python `int` is, and NumPy numbers are converted to strings the same way Python numbers are.

### Steps to reproduce

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go

df = pd.DataFrame({"year": [2020, 2021], "v": [1, 2]})

for label, call in [
    ("name", lambda: go.Scatter(name=df.year.unique()[0])),
    ("text", lambda: go.Scatter(text=np.float32(1.5))),
    ("nticks", lambda: go.Layout(xaxis_nticks=np.int64(5))),
    ("nbinsx", lambda: go.Histogram(nbinsx=np.int32(10))),
]:
    try:
        call()
        print(label, "ok")
    except ValueError as error:
        print(label, str(error).splitlines()[1].strip())
```

Actual:

```text
name Invalid value of type 'numpy.int64' received for the 'name' property of scatter
text Invalid value of type 'numpy.float32' received for the 'text' property of scatter
nticks Invalid value of type 'numpy.int64' received for the 'nticks' property of layout.xaxis
nbinsx Invalid value of type 'numpy.int32' received for the 'nbinsx' property of histogram
```

Expected:

```text
name ok
text ok
nticks ok
nbinsx ok
```

### Notes

`IntegerValidator` checks `isinstance(v, int)` and `StringValidator` checks `isinstance(v, (int, float))`. NumPy integer types are not subclasses of `int`, so they fail both checks, while `NumberValidator` checks `numbers.Number` and accepts them. The error message for string properties says "A number that will be converted to a string", which a NumPy number is.

Reproduced with plotly 7.1.0 and current `main` (`38374acd`), NumPy 2.x, Python 3.12.

comments.body:
Run the following function as a temporary fix.

```python
def fix_widget_error():
    """
    Fix FigureWidget - 'mapbox._derived' Value Error.
    Adopted from: https://github.com/plotly/plotly.py/issues/2570#issuecomment-738735816
    """
    import shutil
    import pkg_resources

    pkg_dir = os.path.dirname(pkg_resources.resource_filename("plotly", "plotly.py"))

    basedatatypesPath = os.path.join(pkg_dir, "basedatatypes.py")

    backup_file = basedatatypesPath.replace(".py", "_bk.py")
    shutil.copyfile(basedatatypesPath, backup_file)

    # read basedatatypes.py
    with open(basedatatypesPath, "r") as f:
        lines = f.read()

    find = "if not BaseFigure._is_key_path_compatible(key_path_str, self.layout):"

    replace = """if not BaseFigure._is_key_path_compatible(key_path_str, self.layout):
                if key_path_str == "mapbox._derived":
                    return"""

    # add new text
    lines = lines.replace(find, replace)

    # overwrite old 'basedatatypes.py'
    with open(basedatatypesPath, "w") as f:
        f.write(lines)
```
